summary: You sit bottom of the table on 80 points, so your GW4 claims process first when the window opens (waivers close 11 September). Palace boss Pierre Sage confirmed today that Mateta is out three weeks with a hamstring injury, removing Strand Larsen's only rival for the striker spot - he was already starting, but this is worth knowing since the model's 0.74 availability figure understates how secure the role now is. The same three claims as last run survive a fresh sweep: Le Fee for Barcola (still bench-bound for his Liverpool debut this afternoon), Rayan for Doku (still out for today's Coventry game with no fresh return-date news), and Igor Jesus for Marmoush, though that last one has weakened to a pure numbers swap between two now-confirmed starters and drops to low confidence. The rest of the squad (Milenkovic, Bijol, Gvardiol, Collins, Schade, Tavernier, Garner, Munoz) are established starters clear of any fresh injury concern, so no fourth or fifth claim clears the bar this week.

claims.why: Barcola is still expected among the substitutes for his Liverpool debut against Ipswich this afternoon, with the latest team news having him in the squad but not the starting XI. Le Fee remains a confirmed Sunderland starter in an advanced midfield role, so this is a bench-bound marquee name for a nailed-on regular starter while Barcola finds his feet.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 16.1 (avail 1.00) versus Barcola at 1.4 (avail 0.10) - the model has no career data on Barcola yet so it is essentially guessing zero, and today's team news still supports treating him as a bench option for now.

claims.why: Doku remains sidelined with the calf injury from City's Community Shield defeat to Arsenal and misses today's game against Coventry, with no permitted outlet giving a firmer return date than the original two-to-three-week estimate that has already elapsed once without him featuring. Rayan is a confirmed Bournemouth starter behind Evanilson and gives a real points floor while Doku's timeline stays unresolved.
claims.model: Model has Rayan at next5 15.8 (avail 0.95) versus Doku at 3.5 (avail 0.00) - the model already prices in the injury, and today's news (still out, no fresh date) does not move that number either way.

claims.why: Both players are now confirmed starters - Igor Jesus is again Forest's central striker in today's lineup, and Marmoush has started every game since his loan move to Tottenham - so the bench-risk case for dropping Marmoush that existed a week ago is gone. This is now a pure model-value swap between two starters, and Marmoush is a full Egypt international with more pedigree than his small Spurs sample suggests, so it is a lower-conviction call than the other two claims.
claims.model: Model has Igor Jesus at next5 14.3 (avail 0.95) versus Marmoush at 8.5 (avail 0.52) - a real gap on paper, but with both players confirmed starting, part of that gap is likely the same new-signing discount that hits every mid-season arrival, so confidence is lower than a fitness-based swap.

claims.why: Woltemade left Newcastle for Juventus on a season-long loan on deadline day, so he plays in Serie A, not the Premier League, until at least next summer - a mandatory drop, not a judgement call. Igor Jesus is confirmed as Forest's starting striker in their predicted XI for Friday's game against Tottenham.
claims.model: Model: Igor Jesus next5 14.5 vs Woltemade 0.3, +14.2. Fully agree - the loan has pushed Woltemade's number to essentially zero, the clearest drop in the squad.

claims.why: Eze is still stuck behind Arsenal's front line under Arteta with no sign of a minutes trend pointing up. Rayan is confirmed in Bournemouth's predicted attacking three alongside Kluivert and Tavernier for the Newcastle game, and is being talked up as a breakout name this season.
claims.model: Model: Rayan next5 16.2 vs Eze 8.0, +8.2. Agree with the model - Eze's bench role explains the gap and there is no sign of it closing.

claims.why: This is a hedge, not an urgent need. Garner's recovery from groin surgery is running ahead of schedule and he started for Everton in midweek against Preston, but Moyes still is not trusting him for a full 90 minutes. Gross is a fully fit, nailed-on Brighton starter with no fitness question at all. Only use this claim if you want the safer floor rather than Garner's upside.
claims.model: Model: Gross next5 16.0 vs Garner 10.1, +5.9. Partial overrule - the model cannot see Garner's accelerated recovery, so the real gap is probably smaller than 5.9, but Gross is nailed and Garner still is not.
